title: Helium-3 scarcity for aneutronic fusion propulsion
bottleneck: The cleanest fusion reactions for spacecraft (deuterium-helium-3) produce few neutrons, sparing the ship from massive shielding — but helium-3 is vanishingly rare on Earth and exists on the Moon only in parts-per-billion concentrations implanted by the solar wind. Harvesting useful quantities would require strip-mining vast areas of regolith with machinery that does not exist, for a fusion reactor that also does not exist. The fuel cycle and the engine are both unsolved, and each depends on the other.
why_it_blocks: Without an accessible fuel supply, even a working fusion drive could not be fueled; the helium-3 economy is a prerequisite bottleneck stacked on top of the reactor bottleneck.
current_state: No helium-3 extraction has ever been attempted; lunar resource plans focus on water and oxygen. Fusion research overwhelmingly targets deuterium-tritium for terrestrial power, not D-He3 for space.
